Order of the Mysteries
General Instructions
1. According to the tradition of our rite, worship is directed toward the east (Abdisho:
The Pearl, discourse 5, chapter 1). For this reason, the church is built from east to west.
On the eastern side stands the sanctuary, three steps above the chancel; and the rest of the church, the nave,
is one step lower, where the faithful gather. The right side of the altar faces north, and its left side faces south.
A curtain separates the sanctuary from the chancel. On the eastern side of the sanctuary
stands the holy table, that is, the altar of atonement, on which the offering is presented.
On its right is placed the holy Gospel, in its center the victorious cross, and on its left the book of the Order of the Mysteries.
Apart from these, nothing else may be placed there unless it is needed for the service of the Mysteries, that is, the Eucharist.
The chalice is prepared in the treasury on the south, that is, on the left, together with the wiping cloth and water;

the paten, however, in the one on the north, that is, on the right.
2. Together with the celebrating priest, an archdeacon serves at the solemn Eucharistic service
and two servers (deacons). The archdeacon is a priest and wears vestments like those of the celebrating priest:
I mean an alb, a cincture, a stole, cuffs, and a chasuble.
The servers wear an alb, a cincture, and a stole. If ordained deacons are not available,
subdeacons or readers serve. If even these are not available, laypeople,
that is, people who have not received ordination, serve at the Mysteries, wearing an alb and a cincture.
3. At the Mysteries, the archdeacon is permitted to prepare the bread and wine in place of the priest and to place them on the altar, saying the prayers appointed for this purpose.
4. During the carrying of the Mysteries, only ordained deacons are permitted to carry the paten and hold the chalice.
5. After the order of the fraction and of the signing, the priest does not sign in the form of a cross between the eyes of the deacons while saying, 'May Christ accept ...
'; unless they are appointed ministers. And the feasts of our Lord are called 'dominical', that is, those of the dispensation;
those of the saints we call 'commemorations', but they are called feasts when they are celebrated with solemn procession;
while the rest of the days are 'ordinary'. 7. The priest makes the sign of the cross upon himself in this way:
he places the palm of his right hand on his forehead, then on his chest, then on his right shoulder, and then on his left.
8. When the order of service says of the priest, “And he kisses the altar,” this is what it means:
the priest actually kisses the altar or touches it with his forehead.
Or he places his hands on the altar and touches his forehead with them.
9. When they give the peace, the recipient holds in his hands the giver’s hands, which are joined together.
They may also give the peace by having the giver and recipient turn to face each other and bow their heads slightly.
10. When the order of service says, “The priest opens or extends his hands or arms,” this is what it means:
He stretches out his hands (or arms) and raises them, but not above his head, with his palms open.
11. The hymns and melodies are sung by those in the sanctuary—the first choir.
Those on the bema form the second choir, and the whole congregation joins them. Otherwise, the congregation is divided into two choirs.
12. The choir helps the people to sing.
Know that new songs of praise or hymns may not be used without permission from the church authorities.
13. When the priest recites a prayer of inclination, he bows his head slightly, with his palms joined together. His voice is quiet but audible to the congregation.
14. The Gospel, the readings, and the Epistle are read on the bema set up in the middle of the nave, or in the chancel. The priest stands there in a place slightly higher than the bema.
On the north side (the right), seats are placed for the priest and the archdeacon; those for the deacons are on the south side (the left).
15. The bread and wine are prepared whenever they are brought to the altar: either while the litanies are being said,
or before the Qudasha begins. 16. The priest does not need to strike the pilasa [?] against the chalice, saying:
'By your command, our Lord and our God.' 17. The first three supplications (kushape) are not to be omitted except out of necessity.
18. The asterisk (܀) indicates a rite or prayers proper to the Eucharist.

The Order of the Eucharistic Liturgies
The priest washes his hands and puts on the sacred vestments without saying anything.
The vestments are: the alb, the cincture, the stole, the cuffs, and the cope.
The deacons and subdeacons wear the alb, cincture, and stole. The others who serve wear only the alb and cincture.
They all go in procession to the sanctuary, carrying the cross and the Gospel book, with a censer and lights, as is customary.
The priest stands in the middle of the sanctuary, facing the holy table.
After placing the cross and the Gospel book in their places, the deacons and the others stand behind the priest.

They all bow together.
The priest says aloud: “Your command.”
They respond: “The command of Christ.”

Then the priest begins: “Glory to God in the highest.” Three times.
After each time they respond: “Amen.”
The priest continues: “And on earth peace, and good hope for humankind, at all times and forever.”

Amen.
And they respond: Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come.
Holy, holy, holy are you, our Father in heaven. Heaven and earth are full of the greatness of your glory.
The watchful angels and human beings cry out to you: Holy, holy, holy are you. Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy.
May your kingdom come; may your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today the bread we need.
And forgive us our debts and our sins, as we too have forgiven
our debtors. And do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.
For yours are the kingdom, the power, and the glory forever and ever. Amen.

Priest: Glory to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
And they respond: From eternity to eternity. Amen and amen.
And they continue: Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy; may your kingdom come. Holy, holy, holy are you, our Father in heaven,
whose great glory fills heaven and earth. The watchful angels and human beings cry out to you: Holy, holy, holy are you.

Deacon: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
And the priest says aloud the prayer before the psalmody.

For Sundays and feasts.
Our Lord and our God, in your compassion strengthen our weakness, so that we may minister the holy mysteries that were given for the renewal and salvation of our nature,
through the mercy of your beloved Son, the Lord of all, forever.

For feasts of the Lord.
Our Lord and our God, strengthen those who rightly believe in your name and truly profess an undistorted confession of faith,
to minister in holiness the mysteries [?] that grant forgiveness and sanctify their souls and bodies,
and to serve you as priests in purity, with hearts and minds cleansed of defilements and far removed from thoughts that stain,
and continually to praise you for the salvation you have bestowed on us through the abundant mercies of your grace,
Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

For commemorations and ordinary days.
May worship, praise, honor, thanksgiving, exaltation, and blessing be given
in heaven and on earth to the worshipful and praiseworthy name of your glorious Trinity at all times, Lord of all,

Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
And they respond: Amen.
And the priest begins the psalmody of the day.

On ordinary days, however, he says:
Psalm 15. Priest: Lord, who may dwell in your tent, and who may live on your holy mountain?
Refrain: Our Lord, set me before your altar with pure thoughts.
Lord, who may dwell in your tent, and who may live on your holy mountain?
Deacon: The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right, who speaks truth in his heart and is not deceitful with his tongue.
Priest: He does no harm to his companion and accepts no bribe against his neighbor.
Deacon: A troublemaker is despised in his eyes, but he honors those who fear the Lord.
Priest: He swears to his companion and does not lie, and he does not lend his money at interest.
Deacon: He takes no bribe against the innocent. Whoever does these things is righteous and will never be shaken.

Priest: Psalm 150. Praise the Lord in his sanctuary; praise him in the firmament of his strength.
Deacon:

Praise him for his mighty power; praise him for his abundant greatness.
Priest: Praise him with the sound of the horn.

Praise him with lyres and harps.
Deacon: Praise him with tambourines and drums; praise him with sweet-sounding strings.

Priest: Praise him with resounding cymbals; praise him with sound and shouting.
Deacon: With every breath let us praise the Lord.
Priest: Psalm 116. Praise the Lord, all you peoples; praise him, all nations.
Deacon: For his grace toward us has grown strong; truly, the Lord is forever.
Priest: Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen.
With purity of thought, our Lord, set me before your altar.
Deacon: Lord, who may dwell in your tent, and who may live on your holy mountain?

How beautiful and glorious is your sanctuary, O God who makes all things holy.
The deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.

The priest prays.
Prayer before the Anthem of the Sanctuary
For Sundays and Feasts
Before the glorious throne of your greatness, my Lord,
and the high and exalted seat of your honor, and the awesome judgment seat of the might of your love, and the atoning altar established by your command,
and the place where your glory dwells, we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, together with the thousands of cherubim who praise you,
and the myriads of seraphim and archangels who proclaim your holiness, kneel and worship,

and give thanks and praise at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They respond: Amen.

For Feasts of the Lord
Before the awesome judgment seat of your greatness and the exalted throne of your divinity,
and the splendid seat of your honor and the glorious chair of your lordship, where the cherubim who serve you offer praise continually,
and the seraphim who praise you proclaim your holiness without ceasing, we kneel in fear and worship with trembling,
and give thanks and praise without ceasing at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

They respond: Amen.
For Commemorations
To the great, awesome, holy, blessed, blissful, and incomprehensible name of your glorious Trinity,
and for your grace toward our race, we owe thanksgiving, worship, and praise at all times, Lord of all.

Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They respond: Amen.
Then they say the sanctuary anthem for the day:
The deacon brings forward the censer and the incense, and the priest blesses the incense, saying quietly:
In the name of your glorious Trinity, may this incense that we offer in your honor be blessed,
so that it may be pleasing to you and bring forgiveness of the sins of the sheep of your flock, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

Amen.
The priest takes three grains of frankincense, places them on the coals in the censer, and makes the sign of the cross over them.
The minister brings the cross and gives it to the celebrant, who receives it with a kiss.
He holds it out to the archdeacon and the other ministers, and also to the faithful,

so that they may kiss it as is fitting. At the end, the minister says: Peace be with us.
The priest says the prayer “For you are Lord”:

On Sundays and feast days:
And when, our Lord and our God, the pleasant fragrance of the sweetness of your love wafts among us,
and our souls are enlightened by the knowledge of your truth, may we be worthy to receive the revelation of your beloved Son from heaven,
and there may we thank and praise you without ceasing in your crowned Church, filled with every help and every blessing. For you are the Lord and Creator of all, forever.

They respond: Amen.
For commemorations and ordinary days:
And for all your help and kindness toward us, which we cannot repay,
we will thank and praise you without ceasing in your crowned Church, filled with every help and every blessing,

for you are the Lord and Creator of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They respond: Amen.
They open the sanctuary curtain, and the deacon censes the sanctuary, beginning on the south side and moving toward the north.
At the end, standing at the sanctuary entrance, he censes the people.
The priest goes with the ministers and the other deacons to the raised platform, carrying the cross, the Gospel book, the censer, and the lights.

They say:
You, Lord of all, we thank; and you, Jesus Christ, we praise,

for you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls.
The others continue:

On Sundays and feast days: It is good to give thanks to the Lord and to sing praise to your name, Most High.
You, Lord of all, we thank;
and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls.

On ordinary days: I have washed my hands in purity and have gone around your altar, Lord.
You, Lord of all, we thank;
and you, Jesus Christ, we praise, for you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls.

Glory. Forever.
You, Lord of all, we thank; and you, Jesus Christ, we praise,

for you are the one who raises our bodies, and you are the good Savior of our souls.
The minister: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
And the priest says: You, my Lord, are truly the one who raises our bodies to life, and you are the good Savior of our souls,
and the constant guardian of our lives. To you, my Lord, we owe thanks, worship, and praise at all times, Lord of all, forever.

And they respond: Amen.
Deacon: Raise your voices, all you people, and praise the living God.

And they respond: Holy God, holy Mighty One, holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.
Glory: Holy God,

holy Mighty One, holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.
Forever: Holy God,

holy Mighty One, holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.
Deacon: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
Priest: Holy, glorious, mighty, and immortal One, who dwells among the holy ones and whose will finds rest in them, we implore you:
Turn toward us, my Lord, have compassion, and have mercy on us, as you always do, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

And they respond: Amen.
The Order of the Readings
The first reader approaches with the book of readings, to the priest’s right.
After bowing his head to the priest, he stands facing the people and says: Sit down and be silent.
The book of so-and-so. Then he turns toward the priest and says: Give the blessing, my lord.
The priest blesses him, saying: Blessed is God, the Lord of all, who makes us wise through his holy teaching.
May his mercies be poured out upon the reader and the listeners at all times, forever.
The reader reads the reading from the left side of the platform. When he has finished, another reader approaches and says: Be silent.
The prophecy of … or … Then he turns toward the priest and says: Give the blessing, my lord. And the priest blesses him.
He reads the second reading. At the end of the readings, the deacon says: Stand for prayer.
Everyone stands and sings the introductory psalm of the day. The priest begins the first verse of the introductory psalm, and they respond with the second verse.
In this way they complete the introductory psalm, singing alternately from either side, with the refrain.
On the feasts of the Lord, they add: His birth, or his baptism, or his resurrection,
or … let us honor with spiritual songs. Hallelujah, hallelujah, hallelujah.

Priest: Hallelujah (three times).
Deacon: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
The priest prays the prayer before the reading from the Apostle.

For Sundays and Feasts
Enlighten, our Lord and our God, the movements of our thoughts,
so that we may listen to and understand the delightful message of your life-giving and divine commandments.
Grant us, in your grace and mercy, to gather from them the benefit of love, hope, and salvation, which is fitting for soul and body,
and to sing you continual praise without ceasing at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

And they answer: Amen.
For commemorations and ordinary days:

And for the Great Fast (except Sundays):
To you, the wise governor and wonderful caretaker of his household, the great treasury pouring forth
every help and every good thing in his mercy, we make supplication.
Turn toward us, my Lord, have compassion, and have mercy on us, as you always do, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

And they answer: Amen.
At the Eucharist, two deacons sing the hymn of instruction before the Epistle.
At the end of the hymn of instruction, the deacon carrying the Epistle goes to read. He stands facing the people and says:
“The letter of Paul the apostle to N., my brothers.” He bows his head toward the priest: “Bless me, my lord.”
The priest says: “May Christ make you wise through his holy teaching
and make you a beautiful mirror for all who listen to the word of instruction from your mouth, through the grace of his mercy. Amen.”
While he reads the Epistle, another deacon holds a lamp in his hand. At the end of the Epistle they answer: “Glory to Christ our Lord.”
Then the deacon says: “Hallelujah” (three times), and they sing the chant for the day.

At its conclusion the deacon adds: “Hallelujah” (three times).
Meanwhile, the priest says this prayer over the incense

quietly:
“My Lord, the sweet fragrance that wafted from you when Mary the sinner poured fragrant oil upon your head—
may it mingle with this incense that we offer in your honor and for the forgiveness of our offenses and sins,

Lord of all, forever.”
He also adds this quietly:
“To you, the radiance of his Father’s glory and the image of the very being of the one who begot him,
who was revealed in the body of our humanity and illuminated the darkness of our sickness with the light of his gospel, we give thanks and bow in worship

and offer praise at all times, Lord of all, forever. Amen.”
Then the priest goes to the Gospel book

and takes it up with a kiss, saying:
“Glory to the eternal mercy that sent you to us,

Christ, the light of the world, [?] the life of all, forever. Amen.”
He holds it out to those in the sanctuary so that they may kiss it.
While they kiss the Gospel book, they sing: “Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, may your prayer be a wall of protection for our souls.”

Or, to “We Are Not Ashamed”:
“At the beginning of the books it is written about me.” Repeat.
“The great book of the gospel
of Christ the King, our Savior: four wondrous scribes set down their books through the power of the Spirit:
Matthew for the believers in Judea, Mark for those in Rome, Luke for the people of Egypt,
and John for the Ephesians. And now, in the four corners of the world, behold, their books are recited,

as they offer glory to your great power, Lord.”
“I have desired to do your will, O God.”

The great book … and so on.
Glory: The great book … and so on.
The priest puts the Gospel book back in its place.
Everyone sits down, and two deacons sing the exposition of the Gospel, facing the people.
At the end of the exposition, the priest takes up the Gospel book again.
He holds the Gospel book in both hands before his eyes and prays quietly:
Make us wise through your law, enlighten our thoughts with the knowledge of you, and sanctify our souls through your truth,
so that we may obey your words and fulfill your commandments at all times, Lord of all, forever. Amen.
He stands facing the people, and the deacon says: Let us stand attentively and listen to the holy Gospel. Or: Be silent and keep still.

The people stand.
The priest blesses the people with the Gospel book and says: Peace be with you.

They respond: And with you and with your spirit.
Priest: The holy Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, the proclamation of Matthew, or Mark, or Luke, or John.

They respond: Glory to Christ our Lord.
While the priest reads the Gospel, one deacon stands before him, offering incense.
Two others carrying lights stand on his right and his left.
When the Gospel is finished, they respond: Glory to Christ our Lord. The priest kisses the book and puts it in its place.

They draw the curtain of the sanctuary.
The deacon begins the litany:
Let us all stand reverently, with joy and gladness (on ordinary days:

with sorrow and earnestness), and let us pray and say: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

Father of mercies and God of all comfort, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

Our Savior, our guardian, and the provider for all, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

For the peace, harmony, and stability of the whole world and of all the churches, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

For our country, for all countries, and for those who live in them in faith, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
For favorable weather, an abundant year, fruitful harvests, and the well-being of the whole world, we ask you:

They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
For the health of our holy father, Mar Pope N., head of the whole Church of Christ,

and of Mar N., the metropolitan or bishop, and for all who serve in their ministry, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

Merciful God, who governs all things with mercy, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

You who are rich in mercy and abundant in compassion, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

You who are good by nature and the giver of all good things, we ask you:
They respond:

Our Lord, have mercy on us.
You who are praised in heaven and worshiped on earth, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

You who alone possess immortality by nature and dwell in glorious light, we ask you:
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.

Save us all by your grace, Christ our Lord. Increase your peace and tranquility among us, and have mercy on us.
They respond: Our Lord, have mercy on us.
While the litany is being recited, the priest goes with the deacon carrying the censer to the southern treasury and incenses

the chalice, saying:
Our Lord and our God, make this chalice fragrant like the chalice of Aaron, the pure priest, within the tabernacle:
Lord of fragrant roots and pleasant aromas, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.
Then the priest pours wine into the chalice in the form of a cross, from east to west and from north to south, saying:
The precious blood is poured into the chalice of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever.

Amen.
He mixes a little water into it in the form of a cross, saying:
One of the soldiers came and pierced our Lord's side with a lance, and immediately blood and water came out.
The one who saw it testified, and his testimony is true. In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever.

Amen.
Again he pours wine into the chalice and says: Wine is mixed with water, and water with wine:

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.
They go to the northern treasury, and the priest incenses the paten and says:
Our Lord and our God, make this paten fragrant like the paten of Aaron, the pure priest, within the tabernacle:

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.
Then the priest takes the firstborn loaf, places it on the paten, and says:
This paten is marked with the holy body of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever. Amen.

The deacon says: With prayer and supplication, we ask for an angel of peace and mercy.
They respond: From you, Lord.

Night and day, throughout all the days of our lives, we ask for lasting peace for your Church and lives free from sins.
They respond: From you, Lord.

We ask for the harmony of love, which is the bond of perfection, in the concord of the Holy Spirit.
They respond: From you, Lord.

We ask for forgiveness of sins and for those things that help our lives and are pleasing to your divinity.
They respond: From you, Lord.

We ask for the Lord's mercy and compassion continually, at every moment.
They respond: From you, Lord.

Let us entrust ourselves and one another to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
They respond: To you, Lord our God.
At the end of the litany, they open the sanctuary curtain. The priest stands there on the bema and, with his hands outstretched, says:
We plead with you and ask you, Lord God Almighty: Bring your grace to fulfillment among us and pour out your gifts through our hands:
And may your mercies and the compassion of your divinity bring pardon for the offenses of your people and forgiveness of the sins of the whole flock of your pasture.
whom you have chosen for yourself in your grace and mercy, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

They answer: Amen.
The deacon: Bless, my lord. Bow your heads for the laying on of hands and receive the blessing.
Everyone bows their heads, and the priest, bending down, quietly recites this prayer of the laying on of hands:

On Sundays and feast days
Lord God Almighty. Repeat.
Yours is the holy catholic Church, purchased through the great suffering of your Christ, the sheep of your pasture.
And through the grace of the Holy Spirit, who shares the nature of your glorious divinity,
the ranks of ordination to the true priesthood are bestowed.
In your mercy, my Lord, you have made our lowly, weak nature worthy to be recognized members in the great body of the holy catholic Church,
to minister spiritual help to the souls of the faithful. Therefore, my Lord, bring your grace to fulfillment in us
and pour out your gifts through our hands. May your mercy and the compassion of your divinity rest upon us and upon this people whom you have chosen for yourself.

On ordinary days and during the Great Fast
Lord God:
Extend the right hand of your mercy over the apostolic catholic Church, from one end of the earth to the other,
and protect it from all harm, hidden and [?].
In your compassion, make us all worthy to minister before you purely, brightly, watchfully, and holily.

Raising his head, he says aloud:
And grant us, my Lord, in your compassion, that all of us together, equally, throughout all the days of our lives, may please your divinity through good deeds of righteousness,
which delight and satisfy the glorious will of your mercy,
and that, with the help of your grace, we may be worthy to offer you praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship at all times, Lord of all,

Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
They answer: Amen.

The deacons, facing the people, proclaim one after another:
Let anyone who has not received baptism leave.
Let anyone who has not received the seal of life leave. Let anyone who does not receive it leave. Leave, you hearers. Watch the doors.
But know that wherever there are no catechumens, it is permissible to proclaim other statements suitable here, such as:
Let all those who have been baptized stand in reverence and honor
and have received the seal of life, so that with unity of heart they may approach the Lord’s table.

Order of worship at the mystery
When the proclamation is finished, the priest takes the cross from the archdeacon’s hands and gives it to the deacon.
Then he gives the Gospel book to another deacon.
The deacons go to the sanctuary and stand before the table, facing one another.
The one carrying the cross stands on the south side, and the one carrying the Gospel book on the north side.
The priest and the archdeacon stand on the bema, facing the altar.
The deacons spread out before the priest a veil bearing an image of the cross. The priest prays: “To you, Lord God…”
And the rest as above. When the ministers say the verses, “Whoever has not received…”
And the rest (or something else in their place), the first minister kisses the Gospel book in his companion’s hands.
His companion, in turn, kisses the cross carried by the first minister.
They place the cross and the Gospel book on the holy table. Then these ministers stand facing the bema.
The priest begins: “Let your priests be clothed in righteousness, and your righteous ones in glory.”
They respond, chanting: “When the priest enters before the holy altar, he stretches out his hands in purity toward heaven,
and calls upon the Spirit, and she descends from on high and consecrates the body…” During this interval the priest bows down and kisses the veil
three times, then stands and chants: “and blood of Christ.” He makes the sign of the cross over those on his right.
The ministers say: “Let us enter his dwelling and bow down before his footstool.” They respond: “When the priest enters…”
And the rest. The priest bows down and makes the sign of the cross as above on the south side of the veil. Then, on the east side, the priest chants:
“Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.” They respond: “When the priest enters…”
And the rest. The ministers chant: “From everlasting to everlasting, amen and amen.”
The priest bows down and makes the sign of the cross on the north side.
Finally, he returns to his place. The ministers say aloud, facing the altar and bowing slightly:
“Forever and for ever and ever.” Repeat. “Our Lord Jesus, spread the right hand of your mercy over your people and the sheep of your pasture, and let it rest upon them.
Lord, your mercy is forever (upon your worshipers); do not abandon the work of your hands into the hands of the evil one.”
They turn to face the priest and say: “Lord, fulfill your promise, as you promised your twelve.”
The priest says: “Look, I am with you until the end of days.”
The ministers come down a little toward the priest and respond: “Be with us as you were with your apostles,
through the help that comes from your grace.” The priest says this three times: “Look, I…” and the rest.
Each time the ministers respond: “Be with us…” and the rest, drawing a little closer to the priest.
Finally, they all stand around the veil and say: “And save us from trials, and grant us times filled with peace.”

that we may give thanks, worship, and praise your great and holy name at all times.
All bow down and kiss the veil.
The priest says: May God, the Lord of all, be with us all in his grace and mercy forever.
At the end, all kiss the priest’s vestment. They begin singing the hymn of the mysteries appointed for the day.

On ordinary days: I waited with hope for the Lord. Repeat.
The body of Christ and his precious blood are on the holy altar:
With reverence and love, let us all approach him, and with the angels let us cry out to him:

Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God.
They respond: Let the poor eat and be satisfied. The body of Christ...
The priest washes his hands at the raised platform, saying: May God, the Lord of all, wash away the filth
of our debts and sins with the hyssop of his compassion, and cleanse the stains of our offenses in the abundant sea of his mercy.

Amen.
The priest goes to the repository on the north side and, with both hands, takes the paten on which the eucharistic loaf rests,
raises it to eye level, and goes up to the altar. The deacon goes to the other repository
and brings the chalice containing wine and water and gives it to the priest. The priest, holding the chalice in his right hand and the paten in his left,

crosses his hands and raises them.
The deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
The priest says quietly: Let us offer praise to your glorious Trinity at every [?], forever.

The deacons respond: Amen.
The priest continues: Christ, who was sacrificed for our salvation
and commanded us to commemorate his suffering, death, burial, and resurrection—
may he accept this sacrifice from our hands in his grace and mercy forever. Amen.
He taps the paten against the chalice three times, saying each time: At your command, our Lord and our God. Then he continues:
These glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries are placed and arranged on the holy altar of Christ until his glorious second coming from heaven.
To him be glory, thanksgiving, worship, and honor, now and always and forever and ever.

The deacon: Amen.
The priest arranges the mysteries on the table, covers them with the veil, and says aloud:
Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.
May there be a commemoration on the holy altar of the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God.
They respond: From everlasting to everlasting, amen and amen. Apostles of the Son

and friends of the Only Begotten, pray that there may be peace in creation.
The priest: Let all the people say, Amen and amen.
The commemoration of Saint Thomas is on the holy altar, together with the righteous who triumphed and the martyrs who were crowned.
They respond: The mighty Lord is with us. Our King is with us, and our God is with us; the God of Jacob is our helper.
The priest: The small together with the great—all the departed have fallen asleep in hope of you, that at your glorious resurrection you will raise them in glory.
They respond: Pour out your hearts before him. Through fasting, prayer, and heartfelt repentance, let us seek the favor of Christ, his Father, and his Spirit.
The priest stands with everyone—that is, with those in the sanctuary and those on the bema—at the doorway of the holy place.
He says quietly, while bowing: With our hearts sprinkled and cleansed from an evil conscience,
may we be worthy to enter the Holy of Holies and stand before your altar in purity, radiance, and holiness,
and offer you spiritual and rational sacrifices in true faith.
Then he stands upright and says aloud with his hands outstretched: We believe in one God, the Father Almighty. They continue:
Maker of all things, visible and invisible;
and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, the firstborn of all creation;
who was begotten of his Father before all ages and was not made, true God from true God,
of the same nature as his Father, through whose hands the worlds were established and everything was created;
who for us human beings and for our salvation came down from heaven and took flesh from the Holy Spirit,
and became human, and was conceived and born of the Virgin Mary;
and suffered and was crucified in the days of Pontius Pilate, and died and was buried, and rose on the third day,
as it is written; and ascended into heaven and sat at the right hand of his Father, and will come again to judge the dead and the living.
And in one Holy Spirit, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father (and the Son), the life-giving Spirit.
And in one holy, apostolic, catholic Church.
We confess one baptism for the forgiveness of sins, and the resurrection of the bodies, and life forever and ever.
Amen. At the end, the priest turns toward the deacon and makes the sign of the cross over him, saying:
May God, the Lord of all, strengthen you to sing his praises. The deacon says this proclamation: Let us pray.
Peace be with us. Pray for the remembrance of our fathers, the catholicoi and bishops,
and of all the priests and deacons, celibate men and virgins, and of all our fathers and brothers,
and of all our sons and daughters, and of all the faithful kings who love Christ,
and of all those who have died and departed from this world in true faith.
And for all the prophets, apostles, martyrs, and confessors here and everywhere, that God may crown them at the resurrection from the dead;
and may give us, together with them, a good hope, a share, life, and an inheritance in the kingdom of heaven. Bless, my lord.
And may this offering be accepted with unveiled faces, and be sanctified by the word of God and by the Holy Spirit;
that it may bring us help, salvation, and life forever and ever in the kingdom of heaven, through the grace of Christ.
At this point the priest approaches the altar and makes three
bows, moving forward with each bow. At the beginning of the first bow, he begins to plead, saying:
I give thanks to you, my Father, Lord of heaven and earth, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit,

because, although I am sinful and unworthy, you have made me worthy by your grace to offer before you these glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries of the body and blood of your Christ, so that I may minister to your people

and the sheep of your pasture the pardon of their debts, the forgiveness of their sins, the salvation of their souls, the reconciliation of the whole world, and the peace and harmony of all the churches.
He goes up to the altar, bows down, and kisses the middle of the holy table, then its right corner, and finally its left.
Turning toward the people, he says: Bless, my lord. My brothers, pray for me, that this offering may be accomplished through my hands. They respond:
May God, the Lord of all, strengthen you to accomplish his will, accept your offering, and be pleased with your sacrifice,
on our behalf, on your behalf, and on behalf of the four corners of the world, through the grace of his compassion forever. Amen.
Then, facing the altar again, he says this prayer of supplication quietly:
Yes, our Lord and our God. Repeat. Do not look at the multitude of our sins, and do not let your lordship be repelled by the weight of our evil deeds;
but in your indescribable grace, sanctify this sacrifice,
and give it strength and power to pardon our many sins,
so that when you, our Lord Jesus Christ, are revealed at the end of time in the humanity you took from us, we may find grace and mercy before you,
and be found worthy to praise you with the spiritual hosts.
The First Anaphora, which is the Anaphora of the blessed apostles Mar Addai and Mar Mari, who made disciples in the East.
When the proclamation is finished, the priest recites this first prayer with bowed head quietly, without stretching out his hands, because he has not yet received the freedom to speak openly.

Prayer with bowed head.
We give thanks, our Lord and our God, for the overflowing wealth of your gracious gifts toward us. Repeat. Although we are sinful and unworthy,
because of your abundant compassion you have made us worthy to minister the holy mysteries of the body and blood of your Christ,
while we ask for your help to strengthen our souls,
so that with perfect love and true faith we may minister your gift to us. Repeat: So that with perfect love…
He kisses the altar, then crosses his hands over his chest and says aloud:

Canon
And we offer up to you praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship, now and at all times and forever and ever.

They respond: Amen.
The priest raises his open hand upright above the space between his eyes, with his fingers visible above his head and his palm facing west.
At “now,” he lowers it to a little below his chest.

At the words “and at all times,” he brings it toward his right shoulder, and at the words “and forever,” he brings it toward his left shoulder, his hand extending a little beyond the shoulders as it moves from one to the other.
Then he turns to face west and says, while making the sign of the cross over the people: Peace be with you.

They respond: And with you and with your spirit.
The priest gives the peace to the archdeacon, as customary, and he in turn gives it to the deacons.
One deacon, facing the people, says: My brothers, give one another the peace in the love of Christ.
He gives the peace to those in the sanctuary and in the choir area. Another deacon gives the peace to the people.
The people give the peace to one another. The deacon recites the diptychs.
And on behalf of all the patriarchs, bishops, priests, deacons, and the entire order of the covenant who have departed from the congregation of the Church;
And on behalf of our lives and the peace of the world, and on behalf of the crown of the year, that it may be blessed and brought to fulfillment by your grace;
And on behalf of all the children of the Church who are worthy to receive this offering that is before you;
And on behalf of all your male and female servants who stand before you at this time;

And on behalf of them all and of us all, may this offering be accepted forever. Amen.
Then, turning toward the people:
Let us all give thanks, ask, and implore the Lord with purity and earnestness. Stand attentively and watch what is being done.
The awesome mysteries are being consecrated. The priest (if a bishop or metropolitan is celebrating:
Let him say “high priest”) has drawn near to pray, so that through his mediation peace may abound for you.
Lower your eyes and direct your minds toward heaven. At this time, ask and implore with vigilance and diligence.
Let no one dare to speak. Whoever prays should pray in his heart. Stand and pray in silence and reverence.

Peace be with us.
During this interval, the priest says this prayer quietly.
Lord God Almighty—repeat—help my weakness in your mercy.
And with the help of your grace, make me worthy to offer before you this living and holy sacrifice,
For the benefit of the whole community and for the praise of your glorious Trinity,

Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
When the deacon says “with vigilance and diligence,” the priest carefully lifts up
The veil from the mysteries, saying: As you have made me worthy, my Lord, by your grace, of your body and blood,
so make me worthy to stand confidently before you on the day of judgment.

Amen.
The deacon brings forward the censer, and the priest blesses the incense as above.
The priest censes the altar while standing at its center. Then the priest says:

Proclamation
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God the Father,
and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with us all, now—he makes the sign of the cross over the mysteries—and at all times and forever and ever.

They respond: Amen.
He continues with his hands raised: Let your minds be on high.
They respond: Toward you, God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel, glorious King.

Priest: The offering is being offered to God, the Lord of all.
They respond: It is fitting and right.

Deacon: Peace be with us.
The priest recites quietly and makes supplication.
Supplication
Lord, Lord,
grant us confidence before you, so that we may boldly complete this living and holy service,
with our consciences pure from all defilement, wickedness, envy, deceit, and bitterness.
Sow in us, my Lord, love and harmony toward one another and toward everyone, by your grace and your mercy, forever. Amen.

He continues with this prayer of bowing:
Worthy of praise from every mouth—repeat—and thanksgiving from every tongue,
and worship and exaltation from every creature, is the adorable and glorious name of the glorious Trinity, of the Father
and the Son and the Holy Spirit, who created the world by his grace and its inhabitants by his mercy,
and showed great kindness toward mortals.
A thousand thousands of heavenly beings and ten thousand times ten thousand holy angels bless and worship your majesty, my Lord.
The hosts of spiritual beings, ministers of fire and spirit, praise your name.
With the holy cherubim and the spiritual seraphim, they offer worship to your lordship. Repeat: With the cherubim...
He kisses the altar at its center, raises his hands, and continues aloud: As they cry out and praise without ceasing,

and call to one another and say:
They respond: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty,
heaven and earth are full of his praises. Hosanna in the highest! Hosanna to the Son of David!
Blessed is he who has come and is coming in the name of the Lord. Hosanna in the highest!

Meanwhile, the priest continues quietly while kissing the altar:
Supplication
Holy are you, God, the Father of truth, you alone.
He from whom every fatherhood in heaven and on earth takes its name. Holy are you, eternal Son, through whom everything came into being.
Holy are you, self-existent Holy Spirit, through whom everything is sanctified. And then: Woe to me, woe to me, for I am undone!
For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people whose lips are unclean.
And my eyes have seen the King, the mighty Lord. How awesome this place is!
For today I have seen the Lord face to face, and this is none other than the house of God.
And now, Lord, let your grace be upon us. Cleanse our uncleanness and sanctify our lips.
And mingle, my Lord, the voices of our lowliness with the praise of holiness offered by the seraphim and archangels.
Glory to your mercy, for you have brought those made of dust into fellowship with the spirits.
He turns toward the people, stretches out his arms and opens them, and says: Bless, my Lord. My brothers, pray for me, that this offering may be accomplished through my hands.
They respond: May Christ hear your prayers. May Christ accept your offering. May Christ make your priesthood shine in the kingdom of heaven.
And may he be pleased with this sacrifice that you offer on your own behalf, on our behalf, and on behalf of the whole world in its entirety,
which looks and waits for the grace of Christ and his mercy forever. Amen. The priest recites this prayer of bowing quietly:
And with these heavenly powers we give thanks to you, my Lord. Repeat. And we bless God the Word,
the hidden offspring from your bosom, who, though he is in your likeness, the radiance from you and the image of your being,
did not consider equality with you something to seize, but emptied himself and took the likeness of a servant.
And he became a complete human being, with a rational, intelligent, immortal soul and a mortal human body.
He was born of a woman and came under the law, to redeem those who are under the law.
And he left us a memorial of our salvation: this mystery that we offer before you.
He raises his voice and says: My Lord, we commemorate the suffering of your Son, as he taught us.
On that night when he was being handed over, Jesus took bread:
The priest takes the paten in both hands. In his pure and holy hands, and he raised his eyes to heaven. He raises his eyes to heaven. To you, his glorious Father:
And he blessed +++. He makes the sign of the cross over the paten three times. And he broke it and gave it to his disciples and said:
This is my body, which is broken for you for the forgiveness of sins. Take and eat of it, all of you.
They respond: Amen. He continues: And likewise over the cup—he holds the cup in his hands—he gave thanks and blessed
+++. He makes the sign of the cross over the cup three times. And he gave it to them and said:
This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

Take and drink from it, all of you.
They answer: Amen.
He says: And whenever you gather in my name,

do this that I have done in remembrance of me.
He bows down.
He continues: And as we have been commanded, my Lord,
we too have gathered, your lowly, weak, and wretched servants, to whom you have shown great kindness that cannot be repaid.
For you clothed yourself in our humanity to give us life through your divinity. You raised up our lowliness and restored us from our fall.
You brought us from death to life, forgave our debts, and made our sinful selves righteous.
You enlightened our understanding and condemned our enemies, our Lord and our God.
You gave victory to the lowliness of our weak nature through the abundant mercy of your grace.

Canon
And for all your help and kindness toward us,
we offer you praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship, now and at all times and forever and ever.

He makes the sign over the mysteries.
They answer: Amen.
The deacon says: Pray in your minds.

Peace be with us.
He continues with this hymn of praise: Lift your eyes to the heights above,
and look with the understanding of your hearts. Seek and contemplate the things being ministered at this time,
when the seraphim stand in awe before the throne of Christ’s glory.
All of them together, with a loud voice and without ceasing, cry out praise and glorify the body that is laid out and the cup that is mixed,
and the people plead, while the priest petitions, implores, and asks for mercy upon the whole world in its entirety.

The priest continues with this supplication, saying with his arms outstretched:
Supplication
Lord God Almighty, accept
this offering on behalf of the high priest and head of the Catholic Church, Mar N., Pope of Rome,
and on behalf of our holy father Mar N., the metropolitan (or bishop), who today lead our people,
and on behalf of the entire holy Catholic Church, and on behalf of priests, leaders, and rulers,
and in honor of all the prophets, apostles, martyrs, and confessors, and on behalf of all the upright and righteous fathers who have pleased you,
and on behalf of all who mourn and are distressed, and on behalf of all who are needy and afflicted,
and on behalf of all who are sick and oppressed, and on behalf of all the departed who, in your name, have left us and passed away,
and on behalf of these people who look for and await your mercy, and on behalf of my weakness, wretchedness, and poverty.
Yes, our Lord and our God, according to your mercy and the abundance of your kindness,
Visit your people and me in my misery, and do not deal with me according to my sins and offenses.
Rather, may I and these people be found worthy of pardon for our offenses and forgiveness of our sins,
through this holy body, which we receive in true faith by the grace that comes from you. Amen. Bless, my lord.
He turns toward the people, stretches out his arms, opens them toward the people, and says: “My brothers, pray for me.”

He turns toward the altar.
Deacon: May Christ hear your prayers. May Christ accept your offering.
May Christ make your priesthood glorious in the kingdom of heaven.
And may he be pleased with this sacrifice that you offer for yourself, for us, and for the whole world in its entirety,

which looks and waits for Christ’s grace and mercy forever. Amen.
The priest recites this prayer of bowing quietly:
You, my Lord, in your abundant, indescribable mercies—repeat—make a good remembrance
and an acceptable one of the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God,
and of all the upright and righteous fathers who have pleased you, in the commemoration of the body and blood of your Christ,
which we offer to you on your pure and holy altar, as you have taught us.
Establish your tranquility and peace among us all the days of the world, so that all the inhabitants of the earth may know you:
that you alone are God, the true Father, and that you sent our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son and your beloved.
And he, our Lord and our God, came and taught us in his life-giving gospel
all the purity and holiness of the prophets, apostles, martyrs, confessors, teachers, and bishops,
and of the priests, deacons, and all the children of the holy catholic Church, those who have been marked— + He makes the sign
over the throne, from bottom to top and from right to left—with the living and life-giving seal of holy baptism.
And we too, my Lord—repeat three times—your lowly, weak, and miserable servants, who are gathered in your name and stand before you at this time,
have received through tradition the example that comes from your Son,
as we rejoice, give praise, commemorate, and celebrate this great, awesome, holy, life-giving, and divine mystery

of the suffering, death, burial, and resurrection of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
The priest raises his hands and places his right hand over his left in the form of a cross above the mysteries, and says:

May your Holy Spirit come, my Lord.
Deacon: Stand and pray in silence and reverence. Peace be with us.
The priest continues: And may he rest upon this offering of your servants, bless it, and sanctify it,
so that it may be for us, my Lord, for pardon of offenses and forgiveness of sins, and for the great hope of resurrection from the dead,
and for new life in the kingdom of heaven, with all who have pleased you.
And for this whole great and wonderful work of salvation that you have accomplished for us:
We will thank you and praise you without ceasing in your Church, redeemed by the precious blood of your Christ, with mouths
open and faces unveiled. And he kisses the altar.

Canon
As we offer praise, honor, thanksgiving, and worship to your living, holy, and life-giving name,

now and always and forever and ever. And he makes the sign of the cross over the mysteries.
And they answer: Amen.

And the priest bows before the altar and says quietly:
Christ, peace of those in heaven and great hope of those on earth,
let your tranquility and peace dwell, my Lord, in the four corners of the world,
and especially in the holy catholic Church. Bring peace between the priesthood and the kingdom, and put an end to wars throughout the earth.
Scatter the divided nations that desire wars, so that we may live a quiet and peaceful life in all chastity and reverence for God.

Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory.
And he stands upright and says:
Have mercy on me, God, according to your grace.
According to the abundance of your mercies, blot out my sins. Wash me thoroughly from my wickedness,
and cleanse me from my sins. For I know my offenses, and my sins are always before me.
Against you alone I have sinned, and I have done evil before you, so that you may be proved right in your word and prevail in your judgments.
For I was conceived in wickedness, and in sins my mother conceived me. But you have desired truth,
and you have made known to me the hidden things of your wisdom. Sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be clean.
Or: To you I lift up my eyes, you who dwell in heaven. As the eyes of servants look toward their masters,
and as the eyes of a maidservant look toward her mistress, so our eyes look toward you, Lord our God, until you have mercy on us.

Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us.
And the deacon brings forward the censer, and the priest blesses it, saying: May there be pleasing to you,
our Lord and our God, our prayer and the fragrance of our incense, like the incense of Aaron, the pure priest, within the tabernacle of meeting,
Lord of fragrant roots and pleasant spices, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.

Order of the Breaking and the Signing
And the priest holds his outstretched hands in the incense and says:
Our Lord and our God, sweeten the odor of our uncleanness and corruption with the pleasant fragrance of the sweetness of your love.
And through it wash me clean of the stains of sin, good shepherd who went out in search of us and found us when we were lost.
Forgive me my offenses and my sins, those committed knowingly and unknowingly.
When he says, “Those committed knowingly and unknowingly,” he folds his hands crosswise over his chest.
Then he says to the deacon: Our Lord and our God, make this deacon pleasing to you, as he stands before your pure and holy altar.
Toward the people: Our Lord and our God, make fragrant these people who look and wait for mercy from you.
And toward the altar: Our Lord and our God, make fragrant this altar, which is established as a likeness of our Lord’s tomb, and his throne, and his body and his atoning blood.
He stretches out his hands and says: Bless, my Lord. Bless, my Lord. Bless, my Lord.
Our Lord and our God, the compassion of your grace brings us near to these glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries, though we are unworthy.
Truly, though we are unworthy. He crosses his hands over his chest, kisses the altar, and bows down.
He stands and takes the loaf that is on the paten in both hands. He raises it up, looking at it, and says:
Glory to your holy name, our Lord Jesus Christ, and worship to your lordship,
at all times, forever. For you are the living and life-giving bread that came down from heaven and gives life to the whole world in its entirety.
Those who eat it do not die, and those who receive it are saved and forgiven through it, and live through it forever. Deacon:
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. I am the bread that came down from on high,
our Savior said mystically to his disciples. Everyone who approaches in love and receives me lives in me forever and inherits the kingdom.
During this, the priest kisses the loaf in the form of a cross, without bringing it to his lips, but symbolically, above and below, to the right and to the left, and says:
Glory to you, my Lord—three times—for your indescribable gift to us, forever.
Deacon: His ministers who do his will: the cherubim, seraphim, and archangels stand before the altar in fear and trembling,
and look at the priest (if it is a bishop or metropolitan who is offering:
at the high priest), who breaks and distributes the body of Christ for the forgiveness of sins.
Open for me the gates of righteousness. O merciful one, whose door is open to the repentant, and who calls sinners to draw near to him:
Open for us, my Lord, the door of your mercy, so that we may enter through it and sing praise to you by night and by day.
The priest says while holding the loaf in his hands: We approach these holy mysteries, my Lord, with true faith in your name.
In your kindness we break, and in your compassion we sign, the body and blood of your beloved, our Lord Jesus Christ,
in the name of the Father—he breaks the loaf into two halves from top to bottom—and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, forever.
He puts the half that is in his left hand in its place, not in its original position,
but with its broken edge facing the cup. Then he makes the sign over the cup with the broken portion in his right hand, from east to west and from north to south, saying:
The precious blood is signed with the life-giving body of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father and of the Son—from east to west—and of the Spirit
of Holiness—from north to south—forever. He dips a third of the half in his hand into the cup and moistens it with the blood.
In the same way, he makes the sign of the cross over the body on the paten with the body in his hand, and says:
The holy body is signed with the forgiving blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, forever.
He holds the two halves in both hands, joins them together over the cup, and says:
These glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries have been set apart, sanctified, perfected, completed, united, and mingled
with one another, in the adored and glorified name of the glorious Trinity: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit,
so that they may be for us, my Lord, for the pardon of offenses, the forgiveness of sins, and the great hope of resurrection from the dead,
and for new life in the kingdom of heaven,
for us and for the holy Church of Christ our Lord, here and everywhere, now and always and forever and ever.
Then he places the halves on the paten, one over the other in the form of a cross, with the lower end facing the cup and the upper end facing the priest.
He bows, stands up, and makes the sign of the cross between his eyes with his right thumb.
Meanwhile, the deacons quietly approach the priest, and he makes the sign of the cross between the eyes of each one and says:
May Christ accept your ministry. May Christ make your face radiant. May Christ preserve your life.

May Christ nurture your youth.
They respond: May Christ accept your offering.
The priest loosens the veil wrapped around the paten and the cup, and says: Glory to you, our Lord Jesus Christ,
for although I am unworthy, in your grace you have appointed me a minister and mediator of your glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries.
In the grace of your compassion, make me worthy of the pardon of offenses and the forgiveness of sins. Amen.

He bows, stands up, and says aloud:
Canon
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God the Father, and the fellowship of the Spirit
of holiness be with us all, now and always and forever and ever. He makes the sign of the cross over himself, raising his hand a little above his head,

and the people share in the signing.
They respond: Amen.

The first deacon turns toward the people and makes this proclamation:
Let us all approach with fear and reverence the mysteries of the body and precious blood of our Savior,
with a pure heart and true faith. Let us remember his suffering and take comfort in his resurrection.
For it was for our sake that the only Son of God took from humanity a mortal body and a rational, intelligent, and immortal soul.
Through his life-giving laws and his holy commandments, he brought us from error to the knowledge of the truth.
After all that he had done for our salvation, the firstfruits of our nature was lifted up on the cross and rose from the dead,
and ascended into heaven. He handed down to us his holy mysteries, through which we may all remember his grace toward us.
Let us, then, with abundant love and a humble will, receive the gift of everlasting life.
And with pure prayer and discerning sorrow, let us share in the mysteries of the Church in the hope of repentance,
as we turn away from our offenses, grieve over our sins, and ask for mercy and forgiveness from God, the Lord of all,

and forgive our fellow servants their offenses.
They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.
Deacon: And let us cleanse our consciences of divisions and disputes.
They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.
Deacon: With our souls free of resentment and hostility,

They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.
Deacon: Let us receive the holy sacrament and be sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.
Deacon: In harmony and with our minds united, let us receive communion in the mysteries, at peace with one another.
They respond: Lord, forgive the sins and offenses of your servants.

Deacon: May they be for us, my Lord, for the resurrection of our bodies and the salvation of our souls.
They respond: And for life forever and ever.

Amen.
Meanwhile, the priest says quietly, with his arms outstretched:
Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers, and praised is your name forever.
For you have not dealt with us according to our sins, but in your abundant mercy you have rescued us from the power of darkness,
and invited us into the kingdom of your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ,
through whom you have undone and abolished the power of death and given us everlasting life that cannot perish.
And now, Lord, you who have made us worthy to stand before your pure and holy altar and to offer you this living and holy sacrifice,
in your compassion, make us worthy to receive this gift in complete purity and holiness.
May it bring us neither judgment nor punishment, but mercy, compassion, and forgiveness of sins,
and resurrection from the dead and everlasting life.
And may we all be witnesses proclaiming your glory, pure shrines and holy temples for you to dwell in,
so that, when we are joined to the body and blood of your Christ, we may shine with all your saints at his great and glorious appearing.
For to you, to him, and to the Holy Spirit belong glory, honor, thanksgiving, and worship, now and always and forever and ever.
While this is being said, the priest breaks the body for those receiving communion, if necessary.
When the litany is finished, the deacon says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
The priest says quietly, bowing down: Forgive, my Lord, in your compassion, the sins and offenses of your servants.
And sanctify our lips by your grace, so that they may bear fruits of praise to your exalted divinity, together with all your saints in your kingdom.
He stands and says in a loud voice, with his arms outstretched:
And make us worthy, our Lord and our God, to stand continually before you without blemish, with a pure heart and unveiled faces,

and with the boldness mercifully granted to us by you, so that all of us together may call upon you and say as follows:
They respond:
Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy. May your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us today the bread we need, and forgive us our debts and our sins, as we too have forgiven our debtors.
And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours are the kingdom and the power and the glory forever and ever. Amen.

On feasts of the Lord, however, instead of “And make us worthy,” the priest says:
Let your peace dwell among us, my Lord,
and your tranquility in our hearts. Let our tongue proclaim your truth, and let your cross be the guardian of our souls,
as we make our mouths into new harps and speak with fiery lips.
Make us worthy, my Lord, with the boldness [?] that comes from you, to pray before you this pure and holy prayer,
which your life-giving mouth taught your true disciples, those entrusted with your mysteries: Whenever you pray, pray in this way, giving thanks and saying:

They respond: Our Father in heaven, and the rest.
The priest says in an audible voice:
Yes, Lord, mighty God, good God and our Father, full of mercy:
We ask you and appeal to the compassion of your grace.
Do not, my Lord, lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one and his forces.
For yours are the kingdom and the power and the strength and the might and the authority, in heaven and on earth,

now and at all times and forever and ever.
They respond: Amen.
When he says “now,” the priest makes the sign of the cross over himself. Then he turns his face toward the people and makes the sign of the cross over them, saying: Peace be with you.

They respond: And with you and with your spirit.
The priest bows slightly and turns toward the altar, saying:

The holy gift is fitting for the holy, my Lord, in perfection.
They respond: One holy Father. One holy Son.
One Holy Spirit. Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

On feasts of the Lord, however, they roll the sanctuary curtain shut and begin in the sanctuary the hymn “You are awesome.” Those in the choir area respond, and when it is finished, they open the curtain.
The first deacon stands on the left side of the sanctuary and says: Praise the living God.
And they respond: Glory to him in his Church, and may his mercy and compassion be upon us at all times and seasons.

And they say the response of the bema.
The priest’s reception of the mysteries.
The priest bows, takes the principal host in his hands, and says quietly:
No, Lord, no, Lord! May your body not bring me condemnation, but atonement for my debts and forgiveness of my sins.
And he continues: Sanctify our bodies by your holy body, and atone for our debts by your precious blood.
And cleanse our consciences with the hyssop of your compassion, Christ, the hope of our nature, Lord of all forever.
And then: Lord Christ, though I am unworthy, I bear the riches of your mercy.
And reveal in me, though I am unworthy, the greatness of the power of your awesome mystery, which I receive by grace.
The priest receives the mysteries with reverence and love. Then he bows, takes the cup in his hands, and says:

You have mixed the cup of your precious blood at your banquet for the throngs of your invited guests, O heavenly bridegroom.
And he drinks the blood carefully.
And he continues: And from it you have given me, a sinner, drink. Glory to you forever for your unspeakable love. Amen.

The order for receiving the mysteries individually.
When the deacons approach, the priest gives the body of our Lord to one of them and says:
The body of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the ministers of God, for the atonement of debts.
And he gives the cup, saying: The precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the minister of God, for the atonement of debts. Or:

The spiritual banquet, for eternal life.
And the deacon approaches the priest and says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
The priest places the veil on this deacon’s hands, and then the paten, and says:
May the grace of God be with you, with us, and with those who receive him in the kingdom of heaven.
Then another deacon approaches and says: Let us pray. Peace be with us.
The priest places the cup in his hands and says: May the grace of the Holy Spirit be with you and with us.
When the response of the bema is finished, the deacon holding the cup says: Bless, my lord. And the priest turns his face toward the people:
And he makes the sign of the cross over them, saying: May the gift of the grace of our life-giver, our Lord Jesus Christ, be fulfilled in mercy with us all.

And they respond: Forever and ever. Amen.
And they say the verses of the response for the day. On ordinary days, however, they say:
My brothers, receive the body of the Son, says the Church, and drink his cup in faith in the royal house.
Then the priest and the deacons go to the entrance of the sanctuary, with the priest holding the paten, or a deacon holding it in his place.
And if they distribute the body and the blood, the priest gives the holy body, saying:
The body of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the pure believer (for the pure female believer), for the atonement of debts.
Then the deacon gives the cup, saying: The precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the pure male believer (for the pure female believer), for the forgiveness of sins.
Or: The spiritual drink, for eternal life.
But if a priest [?] or a deacon receives the mysteries, he says: The body of our Lord... Or: His precious blood...
For the chaste priest. Or: For the deacons of God, for the forgiveness of sins. Or, over the cup: The drink...

Order for administering the mysteries together, or the body alone.
The priest blesses the people, saying:

The gift of her grace... and the rest, as above.
They respond: Forever and ever. Amen.
The priest comes to the entrance of the sanctuary with the deacon carrying the cup, and gives the sacrament to the faithful by dipping:
That is, with the body dipped in the blood. He says: The body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the forgiveness of sins and for eternal life.
Know that whenever the sacrament cannot be distributed to the faithful by dipping:
After the rite of breaking and signing, the priest also signs the other portions that are to be given to the faithful with the body of our Lord dipped in his blood.
After the people have received the sacrament, the priest returns the paten and the cup to their places.
Then he bows down and receives what remains, saying: Your living body, my Lord, which we have eaten,
and your pure blood, which we have drunk—may they not be for us, my Lord, a cause of judgment and punishment, nor of sickness or illness,
but for the forgiveness of debts, the pardon of sins, and confidence before you, Christ, the hope of our nature, Lord of all forever.

Amen.
The priest goes to the treasury on the right side of the sanctuary, where the cup had been prepared.
The deacon pours wine and water into the cup. The priest says: Since we have received your body openly,
may your power dwell in us secretly. May we go out joyfully to meet you, and sing your praise threefold,
with the righteous who fulfill your will, Christ, the hope of our nature, Lord of all forever.

Amen.
The priest drinks from the cup.
While cleaning the vessels, he says: Since we have received your body from the paten,
and drunk your blood from the cup, make us worthy, Lord, to sing your praise in paradise with the thief,
with the righteous who fulfill your will, Christ, the hope of our nature, Lord of all forever. Amen.

During this time the people recite a hymn.
On feasts of the Lord:
Strengthen, our Lord, the hands that have stretched out

and received the sacrament for the forgiveness of sins.
Make them worthy to bear fruit for your divinity every day.
Make the mouths that have praised you within the sanctuary worthy to sing praise.
May the ears that have heard the sound of your praises not hear, my Lord, the sound of terror.
May the eyes that have seen your great compassion see your blessed hope again, my Lord.

And the tongues that cried out, “Holy,” direct them to speak the truth.
The feet that walked within the churches—

make them walk in the land of light.
The bodies that ate your living body, renew them with new life.

Our congregation, which worships your divinity—multiply every kind of help for it.
May your great love remain with us,

and through it may we be enabled to offer praise in return.
Open the door to the petition of us all, and let our service also enter before you.

On Sundays and commemorations
Our Lord Jesus, the [?] King, who through his suffering conquered death the tyrant,
Son of God, who promised us new life in the kingdom above,

remove every harm from us, and cause peace and mercy to dwell in our land,
so that on the day of your appearing we may live before you

and go out to meet you according to your will.
With hosannas we will give thanks to your name

for your grace toward our race,
for your abundant mercy toward our humanity, and for your love that has shone upon our mortality.
You have wiped away our sins through your forgiveness. Glory to your name for your gift!

Blessed is your glory from within your dwelling, you who forgive sins because of your mercy.
In your grace make us all worthy

to give thanks and worship your divinity,
and to offer praise to your lordship at all times. Amen and amen.

At commemorations of the departed and on ordinary days
The mysteries that we have received in faith—

may they bring us forgiveness of sins, my Lord.
You are the likeness of the servant and of the Maker, Christ, King of the ages.
Through your body and your blood you have atoned for and forgiven the blemishes and sins of all who have believed in you.
Make us all worthy to go out boldly to meet you at your revelation,
and with the ranks of the heavenly beings to offer praise. Amen and amen.
The deacon proclaims: Therefore, all of us who, through the gracious gift of the Holy Spirit,
have drawn near, been made worthy, and shared in receiving these glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries—

let us all together give thanks and praise to God who gave them.
They respond: Glory to him for his indescribable gift.
The deacon: Let us pray.

Peace be with us.
The priest stands in the middle before the holy table and prays aloud.
On Sundays and feasts:
It is fitting, my Lord, every day—repeat—and right at all times and proper at every hour
to give thanks, worship, and praise the awesome name of your majesty,
because, my Lord, through your grace and mercy you have made the weak nature of mortal human beings worthy to hallow your name together with the spiritual beings.
And may they share in the mysteries of your gift and delight in the sweetness of your life-giving and divine words.
And may they raise their voices in praise and thanksgiving to your exalted divinity,

at all times, Lord of all, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
And they answer: Amen.

Bless, my lord.
And the priest continues: Christ, our God, our Lord, our King, our Savior, and our Life-giver,
who in his grace made us worthy to receive his body and his precious blood, which sanctifies all,
may he grant us to please him in our words, our deeds, our thoughts, and our actions.
And may this pledge, Lord, which we have received and are receiving, bring us pardon for our offenses and forgiveness of sins,
and the great hope of resurrection from the dead and new life in the kingdom of heaven,
with all who have pleased him, through his grace and his mercy, forever. Amen.
And they say: Our Father in heaven ... and the rest, as at the beginning.

But on ordinary days:
Glory, Lord, and honor, thanksgiving, worship, and unceasing gratitude
we are bound to offer to your glorious Trinity,
for the gift of these glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries, which you have given us in your compassion for the pardon of our offenses, through your grace and your mercy, Lord of all,

Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, forever.
And they answer: Amen. Bless, my lord.
And the priest continues: Blessed is your worshipful glory from your exalted dwelling, Christ, who pardons our offenses and our sins and takes away our transgressions,

through his glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries—Christ, the hope of our nature, forever. Amen.
And they say:
Our Father in heaven ... and the rest, as at the beginning.

Conclusion
And the priest stands at the entrance to the sanctuary, a little to the right.

And he blesses the people in a loud voice, saying:
On Sundays, feasts, and commemorations:
May he who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in heaven through Jesus Christ our Lord,
who invited us to his kingdom and called us to his glory and to his desirable blessings, which do not pass away, cease, or come to an end,
as he promised in his life-giving gospel, saying to the blessed company of his disciples:
"Truly, truly, I tell you: whoever eats my body and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him.
And I will raise him up on the last day, and he will not come into judgment, but has passed from death to eternal life."
May he himself bless our assembly, preserve our order, and make our people radiant,
who have come and delighted in his glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries. And may you be sealed with the living sign of the Lord's cross.

and protected from every hidden and visible harm, now + and always and forever and ever. He makes the sign of the cross over the people.
They respond: Amen.

On ordinary days:
Our Lord Jesus Christ, whom we have served, celebrated, and honored in his glorious, holy, life-giving, and divine mysteries:
May he make us worthy of the splendid glory of his kingdom and of delight with his holy angels,
and of confidence before him, and of standing at his right hand in Jerusalem above.
May his mercy and compassion be poured out upon us, upon the whole world in its entirety, and upon the Church and her children, now + and always and forever and ever.

Another:
To him who pardoned our debts through his body and wiped away our sins through his blood:
Praise be to him in his Church. And upon you, his blessed people and the sheep of his flock:
May he pour out his favors upon you and multiply his mercies and blessings toward you.
May the right hand of his providence overshadow you, now + and always and forever and ever.

Concluding prayer for the departed:
Listen, my Lord, to the voice of our prayer. Let our petition come before you, and accept our sacrifices and offerings.
And pardon the debts of our departed, as with the first offering that Abel the pioneer offered, and that of Noah, blameless and pure,
and that of Abraham, who believed in the Lord, and that of Job, who endured afflictions, and that of Elijah, the true prophet, and that of the apostles in the upper room,
and the coins of that widow. In the same way, my Lord, in your grace, accept the offering of your servant (or: the offering of your female servant).
And make him worthy (or: make her worthy) of the bridal chamber of your kingdom, with all the righteous who have pleased you.
Accept, our Lord, his sacrifice (or: her sacrifice), and pardon and forgive his debts (or: her debts).
And wipe away all his offenses (or: her offenses), his own (or: her own) and those of all his companions (or: her companions).
And make him worthy (or: make her worthy), merciful Lord—this poor servant of yours (or: this poor female servant of yours)—of that spiritual bridal chamber.
With the righteous at your right hand, appoint for him (or: for her), from this very day, both rest and remembrance,
and that enduring delight in the glorious and blessed place. And there may he offer (or: may she offer) thanksgiving,
and glory and honor and worship to the one nature in three persons, unceasingly and continually.
And all who have labored in this service today, small and great, and the speakers in this assembly:
May they be made worthy of forgiveness through grace. Bless, our Lord, with blessings this assembly equally, and the house and the people,
and all of us together, now + and always and forever and ever.
Then the priest comes before the altar, in the middle, bows down, and says:
Remain in peace, altar of forgiveness. Remain in peace, tomb of our Lord.
May the offering that I have received from you be for me an atonement for offenses and forgiveness of sins.

I do not know whether I will come and offer another offering upon you or not.
End.
